paragraphs: Designing an antibody for a particular antigen requires coordinating its amino acid sequence with its three-dimensional structure and its interactions with the target. These requirements combine challenges usually studied separately: predicting structure from sequence, finding sequences for a structure, and modeling binding. AbODE addresses this coupled design problem with a generative model.

The model extends graph-based differential equations to represent contextual information and external interactions. Its continuous differential attention evolves alongside hidden interactions within the antibody and between the antibody and antigen. This makes the changing interaction representation part of the generation process. AbODE also produces its output through a single full-shot decoding round.

The paper develops connections between this design and temporal networks, as well as networks for graph matching. Across the reported benchmarks, AbODE significantly outperforms existing methods on standard evaluation metrics. These findings support the proposed approach to joint sequence and structure generation; the stated evidence concerns benchmark performance rather than demonstrated vaccine discovery.
icml-2023-abode-ab-initio-antibody-desig.tldr: AbODE jointly generates antibody sequences and structures using evolving representations of internal and antigen interactions, improving performance across reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Forecasting treatment outcomes from observational records requires dealing with when measurements are taken. Observation times can depend on an individual's characteristics, earlier outcomes, and treatments. Consequently, irregular observations can carry information about the underlying process, and the recorded examples may provide a distorted view of the outcomes a model needs to predict.

The paper formalizes this informative sampling as a covariate shift problem: the distribution represented by observations differs from the relevant prediction distribution. It shows that failing to account for this shift can prevent accurate treatment-outcome estimation. Its general framework uses inverse intensity weighting to adjust learning for the process governing observation times.

The authors instantiate the framework in TESAR-CDE, a method built with neural controlled differential equations. In a simulation environment based on a clinical use case, the approach demonstrates effective learning under informative sampling. The contribution connects a specific source of observational bias to a corrective learning framework, with the reported effectiveness established in simulation.
icml-2023-accounting-for-informative-sam.tldr: TESAR-CDE accounts for informative observation times through inverse intensity weighting to improve treatment-outcome learning in a clinical-use-case simulation.

paragraphs: Generating several language-model outputs presents a tension between diversity and computational parallelism. Beam search and Gumbel top-k sampling can produce distinct candidates, but are difficult to parallelize. Independent sampling methods are straightforward to run in parallel, yet can return duplicates. The paper develops arithmetic sampling to combine useful properties of both approaches.

The method samples through an arithmetic codebook implicitly specified by the language model. It works with common sampling variations and supports highly parallel computation. Under certain conditions, it also guarantees diversity among beam elements. The framework provides unbiased and consistent estimates of expectations under the original model, connecting candidate generation with statistically reliable estimation.

On WMT machine translation, arithmetic sampling more than halves the standard deviation of estimated expected BLEU rewards. It also closes up to 63% of the BLEU gap between independent sampling and beam search. These results demonstrate both more precise reward estimation and improved translation performance in the evaluated setting, while the diversity guarantee remains conditional.
icml-2023-arithmetic-sampling-parallel-d.tldr: Arithmetic sampling enables parallel language-model decoding with conditional diversity guarantees and improves translation sampling and reward estimation.

paragraphs: The paper studies how several agents can identify their best joint action while collecting as few reward observations as possible. Rewards are organized through a factor graph, which describes how actions contribute through interacting groups. The objective is to identify an optimal global action at a prescribed confidence level.

The authors derive a tight lower bound on the samples required for each problem instance and characterize an optimal sampling strategy. Computing that bound directly is difficult because the associated optimization problem grows exponentially with the number of agents. They therefore use mean-field techniques to obtain a computationally efficient approximation, scaling at most with the number of factors times the number of actions raised to the maximum factor-graph degree.

Their MF-TaS algorithm provably matches this approximated sample-complexity bound. That guarantee concerns the approximation rather than an unconditional match to the original exact bound. Numerical studies use synthetic and real-world settings, including antenna tilt optimization in radio networks, to illustrate the algorithm's performance.
icml-2023-best-arm-identification-in-mul.tldr: MF-TaS uses a mean-field approximation to efficiently identify optimal joint actions with sample complexity matching an approximated instance-specific lower bound.

paragraphs: Treatment-effect predictors aim to describe how the effect of an intervention varies across individuals. This paper focuses on calibrating those predictions so that their reported effect sizes are reliable. It introduces causal isotonic calibration, a nonparametric adjustment that can be applied around any black-box learning algorithm.

The authors also propose cross-calibration to make better use of limited data. Instead of reserving a separate calibration set, it combines cross-fitted predictors into one calibrated predictor using all available observations. This addresses the data cost of calibration while retaining a single predictor for subsequent use.

Under weak conditions that do not require monotonicity, both methods achieve fast, doubly robust calibration rates. The guarantee requires either the propensity score or the outcome regression to be estimated accurately in the specified sense; it does not require both to be accurate. The proposed calibrator offers robust, distribution-free calibration guarantees while preserving predictive performance. The central contribution is therefore a broadly applicable calibration layer with explicit protection against certain estimation errors.
icml-2023-causal-isotonic-calibration-fo.tldr: Causal isotonic calibration adjusts treatment-effect predictions with doubly robust guarantees, while cross-calibration avoids a separate hold-out set.

paragraphs: Tree prediction models produce structured outputs whose nodes and connections must work together. The paper introduces CTreeOT for matching two trees when each is conditioned on an input. Such matching supports lightweight adaptation from a few examples at inference time, without requiring parameter fine-tuning.

CTreeOT has two main components. Its alignment procedure extends Sinkhorn matching to accommodate constraints on tree edges, so matching can account for relationships beyond individual nodes. The procedure alternates matrix rescaling with message passing and can be implemented efficiently using GPU tensor operations. A second component reweights nodes according to their relevance, making the resulting match scores useful for prediction.

The algorithm is differentiable and has a convergence guarantee. The authors demonstrate it on adapting Text-to-SQL systems across database schemas, where they report a significant accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art methods. The result shows how structured matching and relevance weighting can support few-shot adaptation in this task without changing the prediction model's parameters.
icml-2023-conditional-tree-matching-for-.tldr: CTreeOT matches input-conditioned trees to enable few-shot adaptation without fine-tuning, improving cross-schema Text-to-SQL accuracy.

paragraphs: Optimizing an unknown function can require expensive, noisy evaluations whose results arrive after further decisions have already been made. Kernel bandits model this sequential search problem, but much existing analysis assumes immediate feedback. This paper studies the more realistic case in which feedback delays are random.

The proposed algorithm has a regret bound that, up to logarithmic factors, grows as the square root of maximum kernel information gain times the number of steps, plus the expected delay. Regret measures accumulated loss from choosing less effective actions. Crucially, expected delay enters additively, without being multiplied by information gain as in the prior bound discussed in the paper.

The improved dependence on information gain also strengthens the part of the bound unrelated to delay. This matters especially for very non-smooth kernels, where information gain can grow almost linearly and make earlier guarantees uninformative. Simulations support the theoretical results. The contribution is a sharper account of optimization performance when observations arrive stochastically late.
icml-2023-delayed-feedback-in-kernel-ban.tldr: A new kernel-bandit algorithm improves regret guarantees under random feedback delays, with expected delay contributing additively.

paragraphs: Some reinforcement-learning tasks are easier to describe as logical requirements over time than as a single numerical reward. Linear temporal logic provides such a specification language. However, standard reinforcement learning can favor short-term outcomes in ways that prevent it from finding policies with the highest possible probability of satisfying the specification.

The paper introduces eventual discounting, which produces a new value-function proxy for the logical objective. Under this proxy, policies can be found that attain the highest achievable satisfaction probability. The importance of the proxy is its connection between a value-based learning objective and the desired probability of meeting the temporal requirements.

A second contribution uses counterfactual reasoning to extract additional training data from existing rollouts. It considers different ways of satisfying the specification, generating off-policy replay data from on-policy experience. Experiments in both discrete and continuous state-action spaces confirm the effectiveness of this replay approach. Together, the contributions address objective alignment and the reuse of experience for logically specified tasks.
icml-2023-eventual-discounting-temporal-.tldr: Eventual discounting aligns value-based learning with temporal-logic satisfaction, while counterfactual replay improves the use of collected experience.

paragraphs: Binary matrix factorization represents a matrix of zeros and ones using two smaller binary matrices. Given a target rank, the goal is to make their product close to the original matrix under squared Frobenius loss, which sums squared entrywise errors. The paper develops algorithms with much tighter approximation guarantees for this objective.

Its main result achieves loss within a factor of one plus a chosen positive accuracy parameter of the optimum, with runtime singly exponential in the rank. This improves on the previously stated constant-factor guarantee, whose constant was at least 576. The rank dependence matters because the rank is typically a small integer, although the algorithm still has exponential dependence on it.

The techniques also extend to other loss functions and arithmetic over the two-element field. These extensions give bicriteria approximation guarantees, so they should be distinguished from the main fixed-rank result. The approach can be implemented in streaming and distributed computational models, connecting the approximation theory to ways of processing large datasets.
icml-2023-fast-1-varepsilon-approximatio.tldr: The paper gives near-optimal binary matrix factorization approximations with singly exponential rank dependence and extensions to streaming and distributed settings.

paragraphs: Randomized smoothing provides certificates that an image classifier is robust to specified adversarial changes. The paper identifies a source of unnecessary conservatism in existing certification methods: they do not use the fact that valid image inputs have every coordinate between zero and one. Perturbations producing values outside that box can be detected as outside the image space.

The authors derive new certification formulas that incorporate these coordinate constraints. Their focus is robustness measured in the l1 norm, which aggregates the absolute changes across input coordinates. Incorporating the valid input region lets the certification calculation use information already available about which adversarial examples are admissible.

The new formulas yield significant improvements in certified l1 robustness without modifying the classifiers or changing the smoothing distributions. Thus, the reported improvement comes from a stronger analysis of the existing smoothed classifier under the image-space constraints. This is useful because the robustness guarantee can improve without requiring a corresponding change to the model or its noise distribution.
icml-2023-improving-l1-certified-robustn.tldr: Using valid image-value bounds strengthens randomized-smoothing l1 robustness certificates without changing classifiers or smoothing distributions.

paragraphs: A multilayer graph represents several kinds of relationships among the same objects. Different layers may contain different information about communities, making it difficult to decide beforehand how much each should contribute to classification. Simply relying on one layer or their union may fail to use the available structure effectively.

The paper assumes that labels are initially available for a small percentage of nodes. It proposes a parameter-free, Laplacian-regularized model that uses those labels to learn an optimal nonlinear combination of layers. The supplied labels therefore guide how the different relationship structures contribute to the resulting assignments.

The learning procedure combines Frank-Wolfe optimization with an inexact gradient and a modified label-propagation iteration. The authors provide a detailed convergence analysis and evaluate the method on synthetic and real-world datasets. It compares favorably with multiple baselines and outperforms each isolated layer in the reported experiments. These findings support learning the layer combination from limited supervision rather than choosing its contribution in advance.
icml-2023-learning-the-right-layers-a-da.tldr: A parameter-free model uses a small set of node labels to learn a nonlinear graph-layer combination, outperforming isolated layers in experiments.

paragraphs: Learning through a long sequence of recursive computations can make gradient estimation difficult, especially when the sequence is processed in short pieces. ES-Single uses evolution strategies to estimate gradients while smoothing the outer loss landscape. This addresses the chaotic behavior that can arise from repeated applications of an inner computation.

Its defining choice is to sample one perturbation for each particle and keep it fixed throughout the inner problem. It does not draw a new perturbation for every partial unroll. Compared with Persistent Evolution Strategies, the method is simpler to implement, and its variance remains constant with respect to the number of truncated unrolls.

The paper establishes unbiasedness for quadratic inner problems and empirically demonstrates substantially lower variance than Persistent Evolution Strategies. ES-Single consistently performs better in the reported tasks, including hyperparameter optimization, recurrent-network training, learned-optimizer training, and a synthetic benchmark. These findings make fixed perturbations a useful design choice for applying evolution strategies to long inner problems using short truncations.
icml-2023-low-variance-gradient-estimati.tldr: ES-Single keeps perturbations fixed across an inner computation, preventing gradient-estimator variance from growing with the number of truncated unrolls.

paragraphs: Large collections of sequential observations often lack the action labels needed for reinforcement learning. Gameplay videos, for example, can be easier to obtain than recordings paired with the controls used. Action Limited PreTraining addresses this mismatch by combining a large, sparsely labeled target dataset with fully labeled datasets from other environments.

The method uses inverse dynamics modeling to infer missing target actions from observed sequences. Pretraining across environments helps this action-labeling model generalize. The authors find that adding even one labeled source environment substantially improves the generation of action labels for unlabeled target sequences.

On benchmark game-playing environments, ALPT significantly improves game performance and generalization compared with other approaches using annotated data equivalent to only 12 minutes of gameplay. The reported benefits persist even when source and target environments have no actions in common. This suggests that, in the evaluated settings, useful transfer in action inference extends beyond simply reusing an identical action set across environments.
icml-2023-multi-environment-pretraining-.tldr: ALPT transfers inverse-dynamics learning across environments to label missing actions and improve gameplay with limited annotated data.

paragraphs: The paper studies clustering when relationships can involve several objects at once and belong to different categories. An edge-colored hypergraph represents this information: hyperedges encode multiway interactions, and colors distinguish their types. The objective is to understand how closely efficient algorithms can approximate the existing clustering framework's optimum.

The authors improve approximation guarantees using linear programming and prove a matching integrality gap. This establishes tightness for the analyzed relaxation-based guarantees. They also obtain new approximation hardness results, which address limits on achievable approximation, and connect the clustering framework to established objectives including vertex cover and hypergraph multiway cut.

Alongside these theoretical results, the paper presents a combinatorial algorithm with a factor-two approximation guarantee and runtime linear in the hypergraph's size. This supplies an efficient option with an explicit quality bound. Together, the results clarify both the strength of linear-programming approaches and the availability of a fast alternative for clustering categorized multiway interactions.
icml-2023-optimal-lp-rounding-and-linear.tldr: The paper establishes tight linear-programming approximation guarantees and a linear-time factor-two algorithm for clustering edge-colored hypergraphs.

paragraphs: Private federated learning must communicate information during training while protecting participants' data. Compression can reduce this communication, but choosing a compression rate adds a setting that may need adjustment. This paper proposes techniques that choose the rate automatically during training, removing the need to set or tune it beforehand.

The methods respond to the error induced during training, using that signal to adjust compression on the fly. Secure aggregation and differential privacy provide provable privacy guarantees alongside this adaptation. The contribution therefore combines automatic communication control with formal privacy protection, rather than treating the compression choice as a separate manual task.

For mean estimation, the authors prove instance optimality: the techniques adapt to the difficulty of the particular problem with minimal interactivity. This theoretical result specifically concerns mean estimation. Experiments on real-world datasets also achieve favorable compression rates without tuning. Together, these findings support the value of error-responsive compression for reducing communication while preserving the stated privacy guarantees.
icml-2023-private-federated-learning-wit.tldr: Automatic error-based compression reduces private federated-learning communication without rate tuning and is provably instance-optimal for mean estimation.

paragraphs: Learning solutions to parameter-dependent partial differential equations often involves evaluating physical constraints on spatial grids. This paper makes those grids probabilistic: it assigns probability measures to the spatial domain and treats collocation grids as random variables to average over. That perspective underpins a class of physics- and data-informed latent models.

The approach uses scalable variational neural processes for both forward and inverse problems, leading to Gaussian-process models of solution fields. To handle challenges created by random grids in inverse learning, the authors introduce Grid Invariant Convolutional Networks. They also incorporate noisy measurements whose locations need not coincide with a fixed mesh.

Experiments cover a nonlinear Poisson problem, Burgers equation, and Navier-Stokes equations. The reported comparisons show significant computational advantages over current physics-informed neural learning methods while improving prediction and flexibility. The central benefit is that the spatial sampling structure becomes part of the probabilistic model, allowing physics constraints and irregularly located measurements to be handled within the same approach.
icml-2023-random-grid-neural-processes-f.tldr: Random-grid neural processes treat spatial grids probabilistically to solve parametric PDEs efficiently while incorporating noisy measurements at arbitrary locations.

paragraphs: The paper develops a semi-dual formulation of unbalanced quadratic optimal transport and studies its stability. It gives global upper and lower bounds on the objective's Bregman divergence, a measure of how the objective departs from its local linear approximation. The new objective has additional convexity compared with the balanced setting.

That extra convexity supports the paper's first statistical-estimation results for unbalanced transport potentials, including super-parametric rates. Unlike the balanced comparison considered by the authors, these statistical results do not require smooth potentials. The formulation thus contributes both a way to express the optimization problem and stronger control over estimation from data.

For computation, the authors use variable metric descent and prove a 1/k convergence rate for strongly convex potentials. In the balanced case, they establish exponential convergence when potentials are also smooth. Their analysis extends earlier results to non-equivalent metrics. A tractable proof-of-concept implementation is evaluated on a two-dimensional balanced experiment and a medium-dimensional synthetic unbalanced experiment.
icml-2023-semi-dual-unbalanced-quadratic.tldr: A new semi-dual transport formulation uses additional convexity to obtain fast statistical rates and condition-dependent optimization convergence guarantees.

paragraphs: Synthetic datasets inherit imperfections from the models that generate them. This paper studies how those imperfections affect downstream learning and analysis. It finds that treating generated observations as though they were real can produce downstream results that generalize poorly to real data, making uncertainty in the generation process consequential.

The proposed Deep Generative Ensemble framework draws inspiration from deep ensembles. It aims to implicitly approximate the posterior distribution over the generative model's parameters. This approach brings uncertainty about the generator into the synthetic-data workflow, rather than basing downstream use on a single assumed account of the data-generating process.

DGE improves downstream training, evaluation, and uncertainty quantification, vastly outperforming the naive approach on average in the reported results. The largest gains occur for minority classes and low-density regions, where uncertainty about generation is greatest. These findings connect the benefits of accounting for generative uncertainty to the parts of the original data distribution where that uncertainty is especially pronounced.
icml-2023-synthetic-data-real-errors-how.tldr: Deep Generative Ensembles account for uncertainty in synthetic-data generation, improving downstream results especially for minority classes and sparse regions.

paragraphs: Federated learning shares training updates, and those updates can reveal private data. TabLeak studies this risk for tables containing both discrete and continuous values. Reconstructing such records presents a difficult, high-variance optimization problem, and assessing a reconstructed table is less straightforward than visually checking a recovered image.

The attack combines a softmax relaxation with pooled ensembling to address reconstruction optimization. It also provides entropy-based uncertainty estimates to help people assess the recovered information. These components address two distinct needs: producing candidate private records and indicating how uncertain the reconstruction is.

The authors evaluate TabLeak on four tabular datasets under both FedSGD and FedAvg. It breaks several evaluated settings previously considered safe, including recovering large subsets of private data with over 90% accuracy at a batch size of 128. These results expose substantial leakage in the tested tabular federated-learning configurations and support the paper's concern about their use in high-stakes applications such as healthcare and finance.
icml-2023-tableak-tabular-data-leakage-i.tldr: TabLeak reconstructs private tabular records from federated-learning updates and exposes leakage in several settings previously considered safe.

paragraphs: Optimal transport seeks maps that move one probability distribution into another efficiently under a chosen cost. Some neural approaches constrain maps to gradients of convex functions, motivated by a theorem for continuous distributions and squared-Euclidean cost. These architectural constraints introduce optimization difficulties and restrict the costs those approaches can handle.

The paper proposes the Monge gap, a regularizer defined using a transport cost and reference measure. It measures a map's departure from desired optimal-transport properties. Instead of enforcing a particular architecture, the method minimizes a discrepancy between the transformed source distribution and the target, together with this regularization term.

This separates matching the target distribution from encouraging economical transport under the selected cost. The authors study the regularizer and report that their pipeline significantly outperforms other baselines in practice. The approach matters because transport structure is encouraged through the training objective, freeing candidate maps from the convex-network architecture requirements discussed in the paper and accommodating a broader choice of costs.
icml-2023-the-monge-gap-a-regularizer-to.tldr: The Monge gap encourages optimal transport through regularization, removing architectural requirements on learned maps and improving reported empirical performance.

paragraphs: Model-based reinforcement learning faces two related difficulties: repeatedly computing a good policy in a learned model is expensive, and fitting the model may optimize something poorly aligned with policy computation. The paper proposes a unified objective to address both, comparing a learned policy with an expert under the true dynamics.

The objective shows that optimizing expected policy advantage in the learned model under an exploration distribution is sufficient for policy computation. This supports a computationally cheaper approach than traditional planning. For model fitting, the objective includes a value moment matching term that aligns learning the model with how it will be used to compute policies.

The authors develop two no-regret algorithms for optimizing this objective. Simulated benchmarks demonstrate statistical and computational improvements over existing model-based reinforcement-learning methods. The contribution is a shared mathematical target for model fitting and policy computation, together with algorithms that exploit a sufficient policy objective to reduce the repeated computational burden of planning.
icml-2023-the-virtues-of-laziness-in-mod.tldr: A unified objective aligns model fitting with policy computation and supports cheaper model-based reinforcement-learning algorithms with gains in simulated benchmarks.

paragraphs: Many machine-learning methods assume that data lies near a low-dimensional manifold, a structure that behaves locally like an ordinary Euclidean space. Real data can also contain singularities where this local description fails. Such departures can lead to erroneous findings, making their detection relevant before interpolation or inference.

The paper introduces a topological framework with two complementary outputs. One quantifies local intrinsic dimension, describing the dimensional complexity near a point. The other is a Euclidicity score that assesses how closely the neighborhood resembles a manifold. Evaluating across multiple scales makes the assessment sensitive to the size of the neighborhood being examined.

The approach identifies singularities in complex spaces and captures singular structures and local geometric complexity in image data. Its contribution is a way to examine the manifold assumption locally instead of treating it as a single property of an entire dataset. The resulting dimension and Euclidicity assessments provide distinct information about where a manifold-based description may be inadequate.
icml-2023-topological-singularity-detect.tldr: A multiscale topological framework estimates local dimension and Euclidicity to detect departures from manifold structure.

paragraphs: The paper studies online classification when experts must be paid before making predictions. Each expert's accuracy depends on payment through an unknown productivity function. On every round, the learner chooses payments and then predicts, balancing prediction errors against the total amount spent through a weighted cost.

The productivity functions are assumed to be Lipschitz, meaning their changes are bounded relative to changes in payment. The proposed algorithm combines tools from Lipschitz bandits with online classification using surrogate losses. This combination lets the learner exploit the classification structure while learning how payments affect expert accuracy.

After T rounds with K experts, the algorithm's total cost exceeds that of a predictor that knows all productivity functions by at most an order of K squared times log T times the square root of T. Its dependence on T improves on the T to the two-thirds order obtained from the standard Lipschitz-bandit approach discussed in the paper. Synthetic-data experiments evaluate the algorithm empirically.
icml-2023-trading-off-payments-and-accur.tldr: An online algorithm learns how to pay stochastic experts while bounding combined prediction and payment costs against a productivity-informed predictor.

paragraphs: The paper investigates how a Transformer can learn from examples in its input during a forward pass. It begins with an explicit weight construction showing that a single linear self-attention layer can induce the same data transformation as gradient descent on a regression loss. This provides a concrete mechanism linking attention to learning.

In experiments on simple regression tasks, trained attention-only Transformers either learn models highly similar to gradient-descent solutions or acquire weights matching the construction. These findings show how the studied Transformers can become mesa-optimizers: their forward computation performs an internal learning process. The mechanistic account is established in the regression domain considered.

The authors also identify ways Transformers exceed plain gradient descent, including learned iterative curvature corrections and linear learning over deep representations for nonlinear regression. Finally, they discuss how induction heads could fit this gradient-descent interpretation. The contribution combines an exact construction with empirical evidence, while keeping the broader connection to induction-head behavior as a proposed interpretation.
icml-2023-transformers-learn-in-context-.tldr: A constructive equivalence and regression experiments show how attention-only Transformers can implement gradient-based learning within their forward passes.

paragraphs: Discrete latent representations describe data using codewords and offer a route to compact, symbolic abstractions. This paper approaches learning these representations from a generative perspective. Rather than focusing only on modifications to the original vector-quantized variational autoencoder formulation, it explicitly models a distribution over sequences of codewords.

A deterministic decoder maps those codeword sequences into data. Training minimizes a Wasserstein distance between the distribution produced by this mapping and the data distribution. This frames representation learning around how a discrete latent distribution can be transported into the observed distribution, making generation central to the formulation.

The authors develop theoretical connections to the clustering interpretation of Wasserstein distance, supporting better and more controllable clustering solutions. On several established benchmarks, the method improves qualitative and quantitative results over other VQ-VAE variants in codebook use and image reconstruction or generation. These findings connect the proposed generative formulation to both the organization of discrete representations and the quality of their decoded outputs.
icml-2023-vector-quantized-wasserstein-a.tldr: A Wasserstein generative formulation learns discrete codeword representations and improves codebook utilization and image reconstruction or generation on benchmarks.
